newsitem.title: USA: No rain for Florida citrus belt - FASS.
newsitem.headline: No rain for Florida citrus belt - FASS.

text.p: There was virtually no rain this week in the Florida citrus belt, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS), said.
Growers are irrigating in all areas with all types of equipment to maintain good tree condition, according to FASS.
The bloom period is over and most trees have had total petal drop.
Caretakers are cutting cover crops and herbiciding to help eliminate some of the trees' moisture competition.
Hedging, topping, pushing dead trees and burning debris continues, FASS said.
FASS said an estimated 6,291,000 boxes of Valencia oranges were harvested in the week ended April 6, up from 4,677,000 in the prior week and compared with 4,266,000 during the week ended March 23.
An estimated 4,000 boxes of early and mid-oranges were harvested in the week ended April 6, down from 16,000 boxes the prior week, FASS said.
